## What the chronicles say [Record]

Not in the record. The chronicles say nothing of a binding at Trakai in 1382; they note only that Vytautas was with Kęstutis in Trakai that summer and that [Birutė](../characters/birute.qmd) later vanishes from them (see [her sacrifice](ev_birute_sacrifice.qmd)).

## What really happened [Saga]

On the night after the Dagotuvės harvest songs, in a tower shrine at Trakai, Birutė hears the [Amber Queen](../forces/amber_queen.qmd) and sees in Praurimė's fire a black Ship. She gives Vytautas an uncut amber pebble, charmed before sunrise, "warm, pulsing", and binds him with five lines of the Five-Voice. The cost falls on him: a scar on his chest, nothing on the caster. She cuts her palm over the amber (ch. 27 recalls it): "Jo skola yra mano skola", making herself his surety. Vytautas answers with a promise of his own, a flame he must keep. The five-voice working tonight is both a vow and a debt, which the book tracks through the pebble's warm, cold and dead states.

## Consequences

Creates [Birutė's Senovės Sutartis](../magic/sutartis_birute.qmd) and [the Last Flame promise](../magic/flame_promise.qmd). Its surety is paid in full at [Palanga](ev_birute_sacrifice.qmd); its promise is fulfilled and then ended at [Vytautas's death](ev_vytautas_dies.qmd).

## Dramatisation

Book I ch. 3 "Gintaro Sapnas" (Birutė; the same night as ch. 1 and 2, Trakai, late summer 1382; the book still reads as autumn).
